3	A **desktop-oriented** planning surface for EdFringeNow, served at
4	`edfringenow.com/plan/`. It is deliberately separate from the mobile-first home
5	site ("Fringe Discover") and does **not** touch it — the home site stays as-is
6	until this matures.
7	
8	> **Status:** Milestone 2 — *favourites → availability calendar → allocated
9	> itinerary*. You upload your edfringe.com favourites CSV export — or search the
10	> programme and star shows one at a time — and the board's body swaps the drop
11	> stage for the availability grid, showing each favourite as a lane across
12	> August. The swap is **only** that body: one card, one count line
13	> (*"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!"*) and one search bar, all in the same
14	> place in both states, so the first show you add never shunts the page.
15	> Scrub a date window — or let *"Pick my best dates"* place it for
16	> a given stay length or the best Sat–Sun weekend — to see **how many of your
17	> shows are actually catchable**. Those catchable shows are **instantly** slotted
18	> into a clash-free, day-by-day itinerary (one performance each, travel time
19	> between them) — no "Plan" button; it re-plans live as you drag the window or
20	> tune the controls (day hours, meal breaks, travel mode, per-day limits, or
21	> click a show name to pin it into the plan — or a day mark to pin that exact
22	> performance). Export as a **CSV itinerary** or an
23	> **ICS calendar feed**.
24	
25	## 100% client-side
26	
27	There is **no server and no build step**. Everything runs in the browser:
28	
29	1. On load, `plan.js` fetches three files already shipped in this repo and joins
30	   them into the catalogue the engine consumes (`lib/hydrate.js`): the compact
31	   catalogue `../data/normalized/shows.min.json` (4,114 shows, each with a
32	   `performances[]` of `{date, start}`), the shared lookups `../data/venues.json`
33	   it indexes into, and `../data/normalized/availability.min.json`, which supplies
34	   each performance's `{soldOut, status}`.
35	
36	   They are three files rather than one so each can be cached for as long as its
37	   contents last — 4 days for the catalogue (948 KB gzipped), 1 day for
38	   availability (149 KB), which is the only one of them that moves through the
39	   day. See
40	   [`shared/data-cache.js`](../shared/data-cache.js) and the caching table in
41	   [`scraper/README.md`](../scraper/README.md). Availability is the one fetch
42	   allowed to fail: without it every performance is status-unknown, which the
43	   grid already draws.
44	2. You upload your **favourites CSV** (the edfringe export). It is parsed in the
45	   browser with the `FileReader` API — nothing is uploaded anywhere. The CSV's
46	   `URL to Event Details` column yields a slug that matches `show.slug`, so
47	   favourites → available performances is computed entirely locally. **`.csv`
48	   only**, and a file that yields no shows for the grid is reported as the
49	   failure it is (the wrong kind of file, or last year's export) — never as
50	   "N favourites loaded". The board and the stored list are left untouched.
51	3. The availability calendar and the draggable date window recompute live via
52	   the pure engine in [`lib/`](lib/); the *"Pick my best dates"* control scores
53	   every candidate window in the browser the same way.
54	4. Your working favourites (the parsed slug list — never the show data) are
55	   remembered in `localStorage` for **3 days**, so a return visit re-hydrates
56	   the calendar without another export/upload. Every change funnels through
57	   `applyFavourites`, which is also what persists the set, so what's stored always
58	   mirrors what's on the grid. Availability is always re-derived against the
59	   freshest catalogue on restore; a stored list this year's catalogue no longer
60	   knows is quietly forgotten. **Clear** (in the board's head) is the way back to
61	   an empty board.
62	
63	Because the page fetches a data file, open it over HTTP (not `file://`):
64	`python3 -m http.server` from the repo root, then visit `/plan/`.
65	
66	## Files
67	
68	```
69	plan/
70	  index.html          the page (one board — drop stage ↔ grid — then the plan panel)
71	  plan.css            styles (adapted from the design mock)
72	  plan.js             page logic — wires lib/ to the UI, no globals shared with js/app.js
73	  lib/                pure, DOM-free computation engine (ported from EdFringeAllocator's
74	                      Python `edfringe/` package; unit-tested — see below)
75	    favourites.js       parseFavourites(text) -> slugs (CSV / URL-list)
76	    availability.js     isAvailable(perf) denylist + time helpers
77	    travel.js           distanceKm / travelMinutes — haversine + per-mode speeds
78	    engine.js           buildIndex / matchFavourites / summarize + scheduling
79	                        (eligibleSlots / withinDayWindow / compatible /
80	                         requiredGapMinutes / normalizeMealBreaks / buildSchedule)
81	    itinerary.js        toCsv(slots) / toIcs(slots) — the CSV + ICS exporters
82	    search.js           searchShows / filterShows facet filters, catalogueVenues,
83	                        matchFacets (the genre/subgenre/venue name suggestions)
84	    __tests__/engine.test.mjs      node --test suite for the engine
85	    __tests__/planning.test.mjs    day-hours / meal breaks / travel gaps / forcing
86	    __tests__/itinerary.test.mjs   node --test suite for the exporters
87	    __tests__/search.test.mjs      filter semantics, ranking, facet suggestions
88	      (run all: `node --test plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs`)
89	  design/                 Fable design mock + notes (reference, not shipped logic)
90	```
91	
92	## The itinerary allocator (milestone 2)
93	
94	`buildSchedule(shows, options)` (in `lib/engine.js`) turns the catchable shows
95	into a conflict-free plan. It is a deterministic **earliest-finish-first greedy**
96	— the classic optimum for "fit the most non-overlapping intervals on one
97	machine" — extended for this domain: at most one performance per show, at most
98	`maxPerDay` shows a day, and every same-day pair kept `compatible` (no overlap +
99	the travel buffer from `requiredGapMinutes`). `minPerDay` is a post-pass that
100	drops any day below the threshold (no trek into town for a single show). Ties
101	break on slug/date so the same inputs always yield the same plan.
102	
103	The plan is **instant** — there is no "Plan" button. The itinerary recomputes
104	live whenever the date window or any control changes. Screen 3 reads into
105	`options`:
106	
107	- *day starts / day ends* — a day-hours window; a performance must start no
108	  earlier and end no later (drag the lines on the schedule, or use the pickers).
109	  A Fringe evening runs past midnight, so the schedule axis is a fixed **09:00 →
110	  27:00** (03:00), the day end can be set as late as 27:00 (default **25:00 /
111	  01:00**), and an after-midnight late show is folded onto the **previous
112	  festival night** — same real time for exports, drawn at the top of that
113	  night's column;
114	- *meal breaks* — lunch/dinner bands no show may overlap (toggle + drag on the
115	  schedule);
116	- *most / fewest shows per day*, *minimum gap*;
117	- *getting around* — walk / bike / car. Different-venue gaps are the greater of
118	  the minimum gap and the **estimated travel time** between the two venues
119	  (`lib/travel.js`, haversine + per-mode speed, venue coordinates from
120	  `data/venues.json`), so far-apart shows need more slack and a bike/car needs
121	  less;
122	- *forced (must-see) shows* — click a show name in the grid to pin the whole
123	  show into the plan, or click a day mark to pin that one specific performance,
124	  even if the greedy pass would drop it (a pin ignores the per-day cap and
125	  survives the min-per-day drop; a specific-performance pin also overrides the
126	  day-hours window and meal breaks). Click again to lift the pin.
127	
128	The grid mirrors the plan: each lane's Status names its own verdict —
129	**✓ Scheduled!**, **☀ Too early** / **🌙 Too late**, **🍽 Lunch conflict** /
130	**🍽 Dinner conflict**, **Can't fit**, **Sold out**, **📅 No dates** — and the
131	board's count line reads *N shows planned out of M selected*. Between two
132	scheduled shows less than an hour apart, the schedule draws a **travel leg**
133	(distance + time by the chosen mode).
134	
135	The named verdicts come from `placementDiagnostics` (in `lib/engine.js`), which
136	attributes each catchable-but-unplaceable show to the control that would rescue
137	it. Where exactly one *kind* of control is culpable the lane names it (a meal
138	break by name, since that's a thing you can drag); a mix falls back to
139	**Can't fit**. The same diagnostics give the day-start, day-end and meal controls
140	their **"⚠ Prevents N shows"** chip (hover for the list, click to flash those
141	lanes on the grid) and mark the matching boundary line / band on the schedule.
142	
143	The board re-plans live, and the change is **animated** so a switch stays
144	believable: a newly placed show eases in, the same show rescheduled flies to its
145	new slot, and a dropped show fades out where it sat — never a card silently
146	mutating into a different show at a different time. Scrubbing the date window
147	tracks the pointer without the transition; **"Pick my best dates"** and keyboard
148	nudges glide the window lines to their new spot. All of it is disabled under
149	`prefers-reduced-motion`.
150	
151	`lib/itinerary.js` renders the result to a CSV (spreadsheet/print) or ICS feed
152	(import into Google/Apple/Outlook), both built in the browser from a Blob —
153	nothing is uploaded. ICS events use **floating local time** (Edinburgh wall
154	clock), right for an on-the-ground festival plan.
155	
156	## Building the list by search
157	
158	The board's other way in — and the only one that doesn't need an export — is the
159	search bar under the board body. It sits in the same place, at the same width, in
160	both states, so starting a grid from nothing and topping up a full one are the
161	same gesture. Everything it opens drops **downward**: the results overlay, and
162	the "Search tools" row of facet chips (genre, subgenre, venue, accessibility, age
163	limit, price — each a chip that drops a panel of checkable options with a grey
164	per-option show count, matching the Now page's filters).
165	
166	Typing often names a *category* rather than a show ("cabaret", "pleasance"), so
167	`matchFacets` (`lib/search.js`) offers the genres, subgenres and venues whose
168	names match **above** the show hits, styled as filter rows rather than show rows.
169	Picking one ticks that value in its facet, drops the query (free text and a
170	filter on the same word would fight), opens the tools so the changed chip is
171	visible, and lists the whole slate. Venue is keyed on the venue *code*, so a pick
172	takes every room in that venue, and a score tie between two same-named venues
173	goes to the one with more shows (the hub, not its satellite).
174	
175	Starring a row runs the show through the same `applyFavourites` path an upload
176	takes, so persistence, matching and the live re-plan all follow.
177	
178	## The computation, ported from Python
179	
180	The availability/scheduling logic mirrors the deterministic engine in the
181	**EdFringeAllocator** repo (`edfringe/favorites.py`, `extract.py`,
182	`scheduling.py`), re-implemented as browser ES modules. Two data-shape notes
183	where the site's `shows.json` differs from the Python model (documented inline):
184	
185	- the field is `status` here (Python read `ticketStatus`);
186	- performances carry no explicit `end` — it's derived as `start + duration`.
187	
188	Availability uses the same denylist as the Python (`SOLD_OUT`, `OFF_SALE`,
189	`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`, …); offer statuses like `TWO_FOR_ONE` /
190	`PREVIEW_SHOW` / `FREE_*` count as available.
191	
192	## Known limitations / next steps (milestone 1)
193	
194	- **Calendar axis is Aug 1–31.** The data spans Jul 24–Aug 31; a handful of
195	  July preview performances fall off the axis.
196	- **The date window is the only filter.** A start-time selector was tried and
197	  dropped — as a whole-stack filter it wasn't useful (per-show start times
198	  matter mainly at the window's first/last day, which is a later refinement).
199	- **Day-cell colours follow edfringe.com.** Each performance mark uses the same
200	  status palette as edfringe.com's ticket day-picker (tickets available, 2-for-1,
201	  preview, free, event-specific, no-allocation, sold out); a day with two shows
202	  renders as two side-by-side segments.
203	- **The empty board carries no placeholder controls.** The old intake "More
204	  settings" block (fake genre chips, min-gap and trip-date boxes wired to
205	  nothing) is gone: the search tools now offer a real genre/subgenre/venue
206	  filter, and gap / day hours / meal breaks / travel mode / per-day min-max are
207	  live controls on the plan panel.
208	- **Data loading** blocks on the catalogue + lookups + availability; the
209	  descriptions sidecar follows lazily and nothing waits for it.
210	- Mobile layout is out of scope for this milestone (desktop-first by design).

## The itinerary allocator (milestone 2)

`buildSchedule(shows, options)` (in `lib/engine.js`) turns the catchable shows
into a conflict-free plan. It is a deterministic **earliest-finish-first greedy**
— the classic optimum for "fit the most non-overlapping intervals on one
machine" — extended for this domain: at most one performance per show, at most
`maxPerDay` shows a day, and every same-day pair kept `compatible` (no overlap +
the travel buffer from `requiredGapMinutes`). `minPerDay` is a post-pass that
drops any day below the threshold (no trek into town for a single show). Ties
break on slug/date so the same inputs always yield the same plan.

The plan is **instant** — there is no "Plan" button. The itinerary recomputes
live whenever the date window or any control changes. Screen 3 reads into
`options`:

- *day starts / day ends* — a day-hours window; a performance must start no
  earlier and end no later (drag the lines on the schedule, or use the pickers).
  A Fringe evening runs past midnight, so the schedule axis is a fixed **09:00 →
  27:00** (03:00), the day end can be set as late as 27:00 (default **25:00 /
  01:00**), and an after-midnight late show is folded onto the **previous
  festival night** — same real time for exports, drawn at the top of that
  night's column;
- *meal breaks* — lunch/dinner bands no show may overlap (toggle + drag on the
  schedule);
- *most / fewest shows per day*, *minimum gap*;
- *getting around* — walk / bike / car. Different-venue gaps are the greater of
  the minimum gap and the **estimated travel time** between the two venues
  (`lib/travel.js`, haversine + per-mode speed, venue coordinates from
  `data/venues.json`), so far-apart shows need more slack and a bike/car needs
  less;
- *forced (must-see) shows* — click a show name in the grid to pin the whole
  show into the plan, or click a day mark to pin that one specific performance,
  even if the greedy pass would drop it (a pin ignores the per-day cap and
  survives the min-per-day drop; a specific-performance pin also overrides the
  day-hours window and meal breaks). Click again to lift the pin.

The grid mirrors the plan: each lane's Status names its own verdict —
**✓ Scheduled!**, **☀ Too early** / **🌙 Too late**, **🍽 Lunch conflict** /
**🍽 Dinner conflict**, **Can't fit**, **Sold out**, **📅 No dates** — and the
board's count line reads *N shows planned out of M selected*. Between two
scheduled shows less than an hour apart, the schedule draws a **travel leg**
(distance + time by the chosen mode).

The named verdicts come from `placementDiagnostics` (in `lib/engine.js`), which
attributes each catchable-but-unplaceable show to the control that would rescue
it. Where exactly one *kind* of control is culpable the lane names it (a meal
break by name, since that's a thing you can drag); a mix falls back to
**Can't fit**. The same diagnostics give the day-start, day-end and meal controls
their **"⚠ Prevents N shows"** chip (hover for the list, click to flash those
lanes on the grid) and mark the matching boundary line / band on the schedule.

The board re-plans live, and the change is **animated** so a switch stays
believable: a newly placed show eases in, the same show rescheduled flies to its
new slot, and a dropped show fades out where it sat — never a card silently
mutating into a different show at a different time. Scrubbing the date window
tracks the pointer without the transition; **"Pick my best dates"** and keyboard
nudges glide the window lines to their new spot. All of it is disabled under
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

`lib/itinerary.js` renders the result to a CSV (spreadsheet/print) or ICS feed
(import into Google/Apple/Outlook), both built in the browser from a Blob —
nothing is uploaded. ICS events use **floating local time** (Edinburgh wall
clock), right for an on-the-ground festival plan.

## Building the list by search

The board's other way in — and the only one that doesn't need an export — is the
search bar under the board body. It sits in the same place, at the same width, in
both states, so starting a grid from nothing and topping up a full one are the
same gesture. Everything it opens drops **downward**: the results overlay, and
the "Search tools" row of facet chips (genre, subgenre, venue, accessibility, age
limit, price — each a chip that drops a panel of checkable options with a grey
per-option show count, matching the Now page's filters).

Typing often names a *category* rather than a show ("cabaret", "pleasance"), so
`matchFacets` (`lib/search.js`) offers the genres, subgenres and venues whose
names match **above** the show hits, styled as filter rows rather than show rows.
Picking one ticks that value in its facet, drops the query (free text and a
filter on the same word would fight), opens the tools so the changed chip is
visible, and lists the whole slate. Venue is keyed on the venue *code*, so a pick
takes every room in that venue, and a score tie between two same-named venues
goes to the one with more shows (the hub, not its satellite).

Starring a row runs the show through the same `applyFavourites` path an upload
takes, so persistence, matching and the live re-plan all follow.

## The computation, ported from Python

The availability/scheduling logic mirrors the deterministic engine in the
**EdFringeAllocator** repo (`edfringe/favorites.py`, `extract.py`,
`scheduling.py`), re-implemented as browser ES modules. Two data-shape notes
where the site's `shows.json` differs from the Python model (documented inline):

- the field is `status` here (Python read `ticketStatus`);
- performances carry no explicit `end` — it's derived as `start + duration`.

Availability uses the same denylist as the Python (`SOLD_OUT`, `OFF_SALE`,
`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`, …); offer statuses like `TWO_FOR_ONE` /
`PREVIEW_SHOW` / `FREE_*` count as available.

## Known limitations / next steps (milestone 1)

- **Calendar axis is Aug 1–31.** The data spans Jul 24–Aug 31; a handful of
  July preview performances fall off the axis.
- **The date window is the only filter.** A start-time selector was tried and
  dropped — as a whole-stack filter it wasn't useful (per-show start times
  matter mainly at the window's first/last day, which is a later refinement).
- **Day-cell colours follow edfringe.com.** Each performance mark uses the same
  status palette as edfringe.com's ticket day-picker (tickets available, 2-for-1,
  preview, free, event-specific, no-allocation, sold out); a day with two shows
  renders as two side-by-side segments.
- **The empty board carries no placeholder controls.** The old intake "More
  settings" block (fake genre chips, min-gap and trip-date boxes wired to
  nothing) is gone: the search tools now offer a real genre/subgenre/venue
  filter, and gap / day hours / meal breaks / travel mode / per-day min-max are
  live controls on the plan panel.
- **Data loading** blocks on the catalogue + lookups + availability; the
  descriptions sidecar follows lazily and nothing waits for it.
- Mobile layout is out of scope for this milestone (desktop-first by design).

input.body:
## What

A show shut out by a **mix** of controls — some performances hitting the lunch break, the rest running past the day end — used to get the muted, unexplained **"Can't fit"** verdict, even though `placementDiagnostics` already knew exactly which settings were responsible (it lists the show under every control that would rescue it on its own).

Now the mix gets its own amber conflict pill, in the same family as the existing "Too late" / "Lunch conflict" pills:

- **Pill** — names the mix compactly: `▲ Lunch + late` (two culprits), collapsing to `▲ Hours + meals` for three or more.
- **Hover card** — spells out each culprit in the user's own numbers: *"No single setting blocks this show — together they do: some run during your lunch break (13:30–14:30); some run past the end of your day (22:00). Changing any one of these would free at least one performance."*
- **Click** — scrolls to the plan controls and flashes **every** setting responsible (not just one), so the mix reads as a mix on arrival.

A show blocked only by *pairs* of settings at once (no single relaxation frees a performance — say a long show spanning lunch and running past the day end) gets the same treatment under an `Hours + meals` label with its own explanation, since it's still a settings problem, not a clash.

**"Can't fit" is now reserved for the true clash/cap case** — room genuinely ran out, and no setting is to blame.

## How

- `laneStatus` collects all culpable kinds from the diagnostics sets instead of bailing to `cantfit` on any mix, and returns a new `combo` verdict carrying them; the diagnostics' `blockedSlugs` is threaded through so the paired-blocking case is distinguishable from a real clash.
- `statusPillHTML` / `conflictTipHTML` / `wireConflictJumps` render, explain, and wire the combo pill; the combo lane also gets the amber `lane--blocked` treatment instead of the muted one.
- No engine changes; existing CSS classes reused, so no style changes needed.

## Verified

- All 206 unit tests pass (`npm test`); `scripts/verify.sh` all green.
- Driven in the real app (Playwright, seeded favourites + prefs): *Tim Key: Loganberry* (performances at 14:00 and 22:00) with lunch 13:30–14:30 and day end 22:00 renders `▲ Lunch + late`, the hover card reads correctly with the user's numbers, and clicking flashes both the day-end field and the meal-breaks block, each with its `⚠ Prevents N` chip.

The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

1	# Fringe Planner (`/plan`)
2	
3	A **desktop-oriented** planning surface for EdFringeNow, served at
4	`edfringenow.com/plan/`. It is deliberately separate from the mobile-first home
5	site ("Fringe Discover") and does **not** touch it — the home site stays as-is
6	until this matures.
7	
8	> **Status:** Milestone 2 — *favourites → availability calendar → allocated
9	> itinerary*. You upload your edfringe.com favourites CSV export — or search the
10	> programme and star shows one at a time — and the board's body swaps the drop
11	> stage for the availability grid, showing each favourite as a lane across
12	> August. The swap is **only** that body: one card, one count line
13	> (*"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!"*) and one search bar, all in the same
14	> place in both states, so the first show you add never shunts the page.
15	> Scrub a date window — or let *"Pick my best dates"* place it for
16	> a given stay length or the best Sat–Sun weekend — to see **how many of your
17	> shows are actually catchable**. Those catchable shows are **instantly** slotted
18	> into a clash-free, day-by-day itinerary (one performance each, travel time
19	> between them) — no "Plan" button; it re-plans live as you drag the window or
20	> tune the controls (day hours, meal breaks, travel mode, per-day limits, or
21	> click a show name to pin it into the plan — or a day mark to pin that exact
22	> performance). Export as a **CSV itinerary** or an
23	> **ICS calendar feed**.
24	
25	## 100% client-side
26	
27	There is **no server and no build step**. Everything runs in the browser:
28	
29	1. On load, `plan.js` `fetch()`es the show catalogue already shipped in this repo
30	   — `../data/normalized/shows.json` (4,078 shows, each with a `performances[]`
31	   of `{date, start, soldOut, status}`). GitHub Pages serves it gzipped (~1.1 MB).
32	2. You upload your **favourites CSV** (the edfringe export). It is parsed in the
33	   browser with the `FileReader` API — nothing is uploaded anywhere. The CSV's
34	   `URL to Event Details` column yields a slug that matches `show.slug`, so
35	   favourites → available performances is computed entirely locally. **`.csv`
36	   only**, and a file that yields no shows for the grid is reported as the
37	   failure it is (the wrong kind of file, or last year's export) — never as
38	   "N favourites loaded". The board and the stored list are left untouched.
39	3. The availability calendar and the draggable date window recompute live via
40	   the pure engine in [`lib/`](lib/); the *"Pick my best dates"* control scores
41	   every candidate window in the browser the same way.
42	4. Your working favourites (the parsed slug list — never the show data) are
43	   remembered in `localStorage` for **3 days**, so a return visit re-hydrates
44	   the calendar without another export/upload. Every change funnels through
45	   `applyFavourites`, which is also what persists the set, so what's stored always
46	   mirrors what's on the grid. Availability is always re-derived against the
47	   freshest catalogue on restore; a stored list this year's catalogue no longer
48	   knows is quietly forgotten. **Clear** (in the board's head) is the way back to
49	   an empty board.
50	
51	Because the page fetches a data file, open it over HTTP (not `file://`):
52	`python3 -m http.server` from the repo root, then visit `/plan/`.
53	
54	## Files
55	
56	```
57	plan/
58	  index.html          the page (one board — drop stage ↔ grid — then the plan panel)
59	  plan.css            styles (adapted from the design mock)
60	  plan.js             page logic — wires lib/ to the UI, no globals shared with js/app.js
61	  lib/                pure, DOM-free computation engine (ported from EdFringeAllocator's
62	                      Python `edfringe/` package; unit-tested — see below)
63	    favourites.js       parseFavourites(text) -> slugs (CSV / URL-list)
64	    availability.js     isAvailable(perf) denylist + time helpers
65	    travel.js           distanceKm / travelMinutes — haversine + per-mode speeds
66	    engine.js           buildIndex / matchFavourites / summarize + scheduling
67	                        (eligibleSlots / withinDayWindow / compatible /
68	                         requiredGapMinutes / normalizeMealBreaks / buildSchedule)
69	    itinerary.js        toCsv(slots) / toIcs(slots) — the CSV + ICS exporters
70	    search.js           searchShows / filterShows facet filters, catalogueVenues,
71	                        matchFacets (the genre/subgenre/venue name suggestions)
72	    __tests__/engine.test.mjs      node --test suite for the engine
73	    __tests__/planning.test.mjs    day-hours / meal breaks / travel gaps / forcing
74	    __tests__/itinerary.test.mjs   node --test suite for the exporters
75	    __tests__/search.test.mjs      filter semantics, ranking, facet suggestions
76	      (run all: `node --test plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs`)
77	  design/                 Fable design mock + notes (reference, not shipped logic)
78	```
79	
80	## The itinerary allocator (milestone 2)
81	
82	`buildSchedule(shows, options)` (in `lib/engine.js`) turns the catchable shows
83	into a conflict-free plan. It is a deterministic **earliest-finish-first greedy**
84	— the classic optimum for "fit the most non-overlapping intervals on one
85	machine" — extended for this domain: at most one performance per show, at most
86	`maxPerDay` shows a day, and every same-day pair kept `compatible` (no overlap +
87	the travel buffer from `requiredGapMinutes`). `minPerDay` is a post-pass that
88	drops any day below the threshold (no trek into town for a single show). Ties
89	break on slug/date so the same inputs always yield the same plan.
90	
91	The plan is **instant** — there is no "Plan" button. The itinerary recomputes
92	live whenever the date window or any control changes. Screen 3 reads into
93	`options`:
94	
95	- *day starts / day ends* — a day-hours window; a performance must start no
96	  earlier and end no later (drag the lines on the schedule, or use the pickers).
97	  A Fringe evening runs past midnight, so the schedule axis is a fixed **09:00 →
98	  27:00** (03:00), the day end can be set as late as 27:00 (default **25:00 /
99	  01:00**), and an after-midnight late show is folded onto the **previous
100	  festival night** — same real time for exports, drawn at the top of that
101	  night's column;
102	- *meal breaks* — lunch/dinner bands no show may overlap (toggle + drag on the
103	  schedule);
104	- *most / fewest shows per day*, *minimum gap*;
105	- *getting around* — walk / bike / car. Different-venue gaps are the greater of
106	  the minimum gap and the **estimated travel time** between the two venues
107	  (`lib/travel.js`, haversine + per-mode speed, venue coordinates from
108	  `data/venues.json`), so far-apart shows need more slack and a bike/car needs
109	  less;
110	- *forced (must-see) shows* — click a show name in the grid to pin the whole
111	  show into the plan, or click a day mark to pin that one specific performance,
112	  even if the greedy pass would drop it (a pin ignores the per-day cap and
113	  survives the min-per-day drop; a specific-performance pin also overrides the
114	  day-hours window and meal breaks). Click again to lift the pin.
115	
116	The grid mirrors the plan: each lane's Status names its own verdict —
117	**✓ Scheduled!**, **☀ Too early** / **🌙 Too late**, **🍽 Lunch conflict** /
118	**🍽 Dinner conflict**, **Can't fit**, **Sold out**, **📅 No dates** — and the
119	board's count line reads *N shows planned out of M selected*. Between two
120	scheduled shows less than an hour apart, the schedule draws a **travel leg**
121	(distance + time by the chosen mode).
122	
123	The named verdicts come from `placementDiagnostics` (in `lib/engine.js`), which
124	attributes each catchable-but-unplaceable show to the control that would rescue
125	it. Where exactly one *kind* of control is culpable the lane names it (a meal
126	break by name, since that's a thing you can drag); a mix falls back to
127	**Can't fit**. The same diagnostics give the day-start, day-end and meal controls
